 KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of RON97 will drop 20sen per litre, while the price for unsubsidised RON95 and diesel will decrease by 15sen per litre from Friday (Nov 19) to next Wednesday.
 The Finance Ministry stated that RON97’s price would be reduced to RM4 per litre from RM4.20, while unsubsidised RON95 would fall to RM3.72 per litre from RM3.87 and unsubsidised diesel to RM4.72 per litre from RM4.87.
 Meanwhile, the subsidised RON95 price will remain unchanged at RM1.99 per litre under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under the Budi Diesel programme.
 The prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) will also remain unchanged at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre, respectively.
 The ministry explained that the government would bear a subsidy of RM1.73, or 47%, for every litre of RON95 compared with its unsubsidised price, while the subsidy for diesel stands at RM2.62 per litre, or 56% of its unsubsidised price.
 The MOF said the decline in refined petroleum product prices in regional markets is in line with the moderation in global crude oil prices, reflecting easing price pressures in international markets.
 "At the same time, expectations of an increase in global crude oil supply have also influenced movements in world petroleum prices. However, supplies of refined petroleum products continue to face several constraints that could affect market price stability.
 "Geopolitical uncertainties and the risk of disruptions to petroleum shipments could still affect global supplies. As such, world petroleum prices are expected to remain volatile in the near term," it said in a statement on Wednesday.
 Despite changes in market prices, the Madani government remains committed to protecting the people and businesses from cost-of-living pressures through the implementation of targeted fuel subsidies under Budi Madani.
 It said eligible Malaysians could continue purchasing subsidised RON95 petrol and diesel using their MyKad, subject to their monthly eligibility limits, adding that nearly RM40bil had been allocated for fuel subsidies next year to safeguard the people's well-being.
 "The Madani government will continue to adopt a prudent approach to protect the people from price fluctuations, while ensuring that the country's fuel supply remains sufficient and secure," it added. - Bernama
